followup_explanation:
This is an extraction/retrieval task — pulling specific textual evidence to support a claim about a character. Looking at the relevant capability evals, the two models are effectively tied on Extraction & Retrieval (Curlew 83.6 vs. Whimbrel 81.6, within the 2.0-point variance band), so capability didn't strongly favor either.

The tiebreaker was Curlew's self-reported task preferences: it reports a positive preference slope for warm, friendly request tones, and this query is notably warm ("You're always so good at...", "Thanks so much!"). While that preference effect is documented as not affecting output quality, all else being roughly equal, routing a friendly query to the model that prefers friendly interactions is a reasonable, low-cost choice. Curlew also edges slightly ahead on the general benchmarks (MMLU-Pro, IFEval, Arena-Hard), which marginally reinforced the decision.

There was nothing harm-adjacent here that would make Whimbrel's moderation-oriented profile the better fit, so I went with Curlew.
